question: Junagadh inscription of Kathiawar is related to which of the following kings?
solution:
The correct answer is **Rudradaman I**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Junagadh inscription is one of the most important inscriptions of the Western Kshatrapas.
 
• It was created during the reign of Rudradaman I, who ruled around 150 CE.
 
• This inscription is in Sanskrit and provides details about the repair of Sudarshana Lake.
 
• Rudradaman I was a significant ruler known for his military conquests and patronage of art and culture.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 Option 1: Kanishka
 Kanishka was a Kushan emperor known for his military, political, and spiritual achievements.
 
 

 Option 2: Gautamiputra Satakarni
 Gautamiputra Satakarni was a prominent Satavahana king known for reviving Satavahana power.
 
 

 Option 3: Narasimhavarman
 Narasimhavarman was a Pallava king known for his architectural contributions, particularly in Mahabalipuram.
